claim: To limit requests to a login page without affecting the rest of the site, you can create a rate-based rule with a scope-down statement that matches requests to the login page and the request aggregation set to Count all.
question: How do you rate-limit only the login page with AWS WAF?

values.display: a rate-based rule with a scope-down statement
without affecting traffic to the rest of your site

evidence.quote: To limit the number of requests to the login page on your website without affecting traffic to the rest of your site, you could create a rate-based rule with a scope-down statement that matches requests to your login page and with the request aggregation set to **Count all**.

claim: The scope-down statement of a rate-based rule can be optional or required, depending on the rule's other configuration settings.
question: Is a scope-down statement always required in a rate-based rule?

qualifiers.condition: required with the Count all aggregation option

evidence.quote: The scope-down statement can be optional or required, depending on your other rule configuration settings.

claim: When you add a rule group to a web ACL you can override the actions it takes on matching requests; the override does not alter the rule group itself, only how AWS WAF uses it in that web ACL.
question: Can you change what a managed rule group does in your web ACL without editing the group?

values.display: you can override the actions it takes
doesn't alter the rule group itself

qualifiers.scope: per rule group in a web ACL

evidence.quote: When you add a rule group to your protection pack (web ACL), you can override the actions it takes on matching web requests. Overriding the actions for a rule group inside your protection pack (web ACL) configuration doesn't alter the rule group itself. It only alters how AWS WAF uses the rule group in the context of the protection pack (web ACL).

claim: You can override the actions of the rules inside a rule group to any valid rule action, and matching requests are then handled exactly as if the rule's action were the override setting.
question: How do you test a managed rule group without blocking traffic?

values.display: handled exactly as if the configured rule's action were the override setting

qualifiers.scope: per rule group in a web ACL

evidence.quote: You can override the actions of the rules inside a rule group to any valid rule action. When you do this, matching requests are handled exactly as if the configured rule's action were the override setting.

note: d009, d106. Exam use: override managed rules to Count while testing.

claim: AWS WAF does not support inspecting very large contents of the request body, headers or cookies, because the host service has count and size limits on what it forwards to AWS WAF.
question: Can AWS WAF inspect the full body, all headers and all cookies of any request?

values.display: doesn't support inspecting very large contents

evidence.quote: AWS WAF doesn't support inspecting very large contents for the web request components body, headers, or cookies. The underlying host service has count and size limits on what it forwards to AWS WAF for inspection.

claim: When AWS WAF allows a request to proceed, the entire request is sent to the protected resource, including contents outside the limits that AWS WAF could inspect.
question: Does AWS WAF cut off the uninspected part of a large request it allows?

values.display: the entire web request is sent

evidence.quote: When AWS WAF allows a web request to proceed to your protected resource, the entire web request is sent, including any contents that are outside of the count and size limits that AWS WAF was able to inspect.

claim: Oversize handling in a rule statement has three options: Continue inspects the contents within the size limits, Match applies the rule action without evaluating the inspection criteria, and No match continues with the rest of the rules as for any non-matching rule.
question: What can AWS WAF do with a request whose body is larger than it can inspect?

values.display: will inspect the request component contents that are within the size limits
AWS WAF applies the rule action to the request
like it would do for any non-matching rule

qualifiers.scope: rule statements that inspect body, JSON body, headers or cookies

evidence.quote: AWS WAF will inspect the request component contents that are within the size limits.
AWS WAF applies the rule action to the request without evaluating it against the rule's inspection criteria.
AWS WAF continues its inspection of the web request using the rest of the rules in the protection pack (web ACL) like it would do for any non-matching rule.

note: d017. The three quotes are the second sentences of the list items Continue, Match and No match.

claim: In the AWS WAF console you must choose an oversize handling option; outside the console, the default option is Continue.
question: What is the default oversize handling of a rule created through the API?

values.display: you're required to choose one of these handling options
Outside the console, the default option is Continue.

evidence.quote: In the AWS WAF console, you're required to choose one of these handling options. Outside the console, the default option is Continue.

claim: If a rule with the Block action uses the Match oversize option, it blocks any request whose inspected component is oversize.
question: How do you block every request whose body is too large for AWS WAF to inspect fully?

values.display: the rule will block a request whose inspected component is oversize

qualifiers.condition: oversize handling Match and rule action Block

evidence.quote: If you use the Match option in a rule that has its action set to Block, the rule will block a request whose inspected component is oversize.

claim: Component size and count limits apply to all rules in a web ACL, including rules in managed rule groups and in rule groups shared with you by another account.
question: Do the body inspection limits also apply to managed rule groups?

values.display: apply to all rules that you use

evidence.quote: Component size and count limitations apply to all rules that you use in your protection pack (web ACL). This includes any rules that you use but don't manage, in managed rule groups and in rule groups that are shared with you by another account.
